Hi Priya — thanks for the heads up and the vendor_form. Looping in Marissa (revenue ops) and Vanessa (channel billing) who own marketplace settlements. Quick answers below, we'll follow up with a checklist and timeline:

- We can support a seller-entity swap for AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces, but it requires coordination with the marketplace operator plus a signed W-9 or W-8BEN and supporting APAC tax residency documents. For EU VAT reverse-charge cases we also ask for VAT registration evidence.
- Typical timeline: 7-12 business days after we receive completed forms and the marketplace confirms the swap. It can be longer if the marketplace needs manual review.
- Attachments we will send: our template W-9 and the channel COA split template (for bookkeeping).

Marissa / Vanessa — can you confirm the exact DocuSign/HubSpot steps and whether we should bill CloudCorp APAC for the May settlement or hold and reissue?

Hi all — process & ask from revenue ops perspective:

1) Documents we need from CloudCorp: signed W-8BEN (non-US entity) OR signed W-9 (if US entity), plus local APAC tax residency certificate (if available) and the vendor_form_request.pdf you attached.
2) Redwood steps: we open a marketplace case with AWS/Azure/GCP, submit the seller-entity swap request, and provide the marketplace the tax docs. We then ask the marketplace for an invoice reissue or credit + reissue path.
3) Accounting treatment: for May payouts we can either: (a) hold Redwood-side invoice posting pending swap confirmation (likely delays recognition), or (b) post the invoice to the original reseller and issue an offset credit + new invoice to CloudCorp APAC once swap completes. Option (b) is our standard to avoid delaying recognition, but it creates extra settlement entries.

Please confirm which path CloudCorp prefers. If you choose option (b), we will need the signed tax docs by EOD 2027-05-12 to meet a 2027-05-20 settlement window.

DocuSign: we'll send the tax form templates via DocuSign; you can also upload signed PDFs to the shared Drive link below.

Priya — good to see the signed W-8BEN, thanks. Answers and next steps below.

On 2027-05-11 Priya Nair wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear options. We're a non-US APAC entity and will provide a signed W-8BEN and local tax residency certificate. A couple of clarifying questions from our tax team:
>
> - For VAT: will Redwood accept a reverse-charge evidence pack (VAT reg + VAT rep letter) so AWS doesn't apply withholding at source?
> - If we go with option (b) (credit + reissue), can Redwood confirm the accounting memo that will appear on the credit so our AP can reconcile against the original invoice? That helps avoid disputes.

Responses:
- VAT: yes — for APAC customers (e.g., Australia/NZ/HK/SG) we accept VAT/GST registration evidence and a reverse-charge pack where applicable. We will forward the evidence to the marketplace and request application of the reverse-charge / no-withholding. Note some marketplaces still perform a manual tax desk review which can add 3-5 business days.
- Accounting memo: if we issue a credit + reissue, the credit memo will reference the original invoice number and state "Seller entity swap — credit for invoice X; reissued to CloudCorp APAC (AP-98765)." We'll include the HubSpot deal ID and our internal settlement reference on the memo to simplify reconciliation.

Recommended path for timing:
1) CloudCorp uploads signed W-8BEN + APAC tax residency doc to the Drive folder now (we have it as signed_w8ben.pdf).
2) Redwood opens the marketplace swap case same day and requests invoice credit + reissue.
3) Marketplace confirms swap (7-12 business days typical) and issues credit + new invoice.
4) Redwood posts credit and posts new invoice to CloudCorp APAC; we will provide an exported COA split file for your AP.

I'll kick off the marketplace case this afternoon and share the case reference. If you need prioritization we can escalate to AWS Marketplace support (cc'ed).
